records.name: Interval estimator
records.summary: A pair of sample functions giving lower and upper bounds for a real-valued parameter.
records.statistical_question_answered: What random set of plausible parameter values is reported?
records.decision_improved: Improves inference communication when point estimates are insufficient.
assumptions_required: Target parameter is real-valued or componentwise interval is defined.
conditions_required: Lower and upper functions are computable.
does_not_guarantee: It does not automatically have stated coverage.
use_when: Confidence, credible, and prediction-style interval construction.
do_not_use_when: When parameter is not ordered or set geometry is not interval-shaped.
common_misuses: Reporting an interval without construction assumptions.
diagnostic_questions: What property does the interval have?

records.name: Coverage probability
records.summary: The probability, under a parameter value, that the random interval contains the true parameter.
records.statistical_question_answered: How often would this procedure cover in repeated sampling?
assumptions_required: A random interval and model are specified.
conditions_required: Parameter value under which probability is evaluated is clear.
does_not_guarantee: It is not posterior probability for this realized interval unless Bayesian conditions are added.
do_not_use_when: When no sampling model is specified.
common_misuses: Saying a realized 95% confidence interval has 95% probability of containing fixed θ.

records.name: Confidence coefficient
records.summary: The infimum of coverage probability over the parameter space.
records.statistical_question_answered: What guaranteed minimum coverage does the interval procedure have?
assumptions_required: Coverage probability is defined over parameter space.
conditions_required: Infimum can be identified or bounded.
guarantees: A lower-bound coverage statement is available.
does_not_guarantee: It does not say every θ has exactly that coverage.
do_not_use_when: When coverage depends on unmodeled conditions.
common_misuses: Confusing nominal coefficient with pointwise coverage.
checks_or_evidence_needed: Analytic or simulated coverage over θ.

records.name: Pivotal quantity
records.summary: A function of data and parameters whose distribution does not depend on unknown parameters.
records.statistical_question_answered: Can a parameter-free reference distribution create an interval?
records.problem_addressed: Provides a direct route to confidence intervals.
records.decision_improved: Improves exact or approximate interval construction.
conditions_required: Distribution is free of all unknown parameters.
guarantees: Probability statements about the pivot can be inverted.
does_not_guarantee: It does not help if its distribution changes with nuisance parameters.
use_when: Normal, gamma, location-scale, and transformed interval problems.
do_not_use_when: When nuisance parameters remain in the pivot distribution.
common_misuses: Using a pivot after estimating a nuisance parameter without adjustment.

records.name: Unbiased confidence set
records.summary: A confidence set whose probability of covering wrong parameter values is no larger than its nominal level for all alternatives.
records.statistical_question_answered: Does the interval avoid favoring false values too often?
records.problem_addressed: Extends unbiasedness ideas to confidence sets.
assumptions_required: Confidence set and parameter space are specified.
guarantees: A form of test-related optimality can be assessed.
does_not_guarantee: It does not make the interval shortest.
use_when: Theoretical interval comparisons tied to tests.
do_not_use_when: When only descriptive uncertainty is needed.
common_misuses: Assuming coverage alone implies all optimality.
diagnostic_questions: What is Pθ(θ' in C(X)) for θ'≠θ?
checks_or_evidence_needed: Coverage under true and false values.

records.plain_language_meaning: Inverting acceptance regions of level-α tests for each parameter value yields a 1-α confidence set.
records.formal_statement_shape: C(x)={θ0: x∈A(θ0)} has coverage at least 1-α.
assumptions: For each θ0, A(θ0) is the acceptance region of a level-α test of H0:θ=θ0.
conditions: For each θ0, A(θ0) is the acceptance region of a level-α test of H0:θ=θ0.
records.conclusion: Confidence sets can be built from hypothesis tests.
records.proof_strategy_summary: Coverage follows because when θ is true, the data fall in A(θ) with probability at least 1-α.
common_misuse: Inverting tests whose level is not controlled

records.result_name: UMP tests and UMA confidence bounds
records.plain_language_meaning: Inverting UMP tests can yield uniformly most accurate one-sided confidence bounds under appropriate one-sided settings.
records.formal_statement_shape: UMP level-α acceptance regions inverted produce confidence sets with optimal false-coverage behavior.
assumptions: UMP tests exist for H0:θ=θ0 versus one-sided alternatives.
Acceptance regions are used as in theorem.
conditions: UMP tests exist for H0:θ=θ0 versus one-sided alternatives.
Acceptance regions are used as in theorem.
records.conclusion: Optimality of tests transfers to a form of interval optimality.
records.why_it_matters: Connects Karlin-Rubin/Neyman-Pearson theory with confidence-bound construction.
records.proof_strategy_summary: Relate coverage of false parameter values to power of tests for true alternatives.
common_misuse: Expecting two-sided shortest intervals from one-sided UMP logic
what_breaks_if_assumptions_fail: The optimality criterion differs from interval length or Bayes risk.
